dedupe_keys.name: powergridworld multi agent reinforcement learning environments for power systems

description: PowerGridworld is an open-source framework for building multi-agent reinforcement learning environments for power systems in which power flow results define grid-level variables and costs. It was released in 2021 by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, with David Biagioni, Xiangyu Zhang, Dylan Wald, Deepthi Vaidhynathan, Rohit Chintala, Jennifer King and Ahmed Zamzam as authors, because existing multi-agent training frameworks could not quickly prototype heterogeneous, multi-device power system environments. Users compose component Gym environments, such as building, photovoltaic and battery physics, into grid-interactive agents, then combine agents into multi-agent simulations where each agent's consumption or injection feeds an OpenDSS distribution feeder power flow; bus voltages and line flows can be part of each agent's observations. The README includes two case studies. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under the BSD 3-Clause licence at no cost, with a latest commit in August 2025. Caveats: it is a research framework with a single early tag, and results depend on the chosen feeder and training settings. Simulation uses are training distributed control policies for buildings and DERs under grid constraints. Related records: platform-opendss provides the power flow, and platform-grid2op is a transmission-level learning environment.
